title: -ir and -re verbs
goal: Use finir and choisir, prendre, comprendre and apprendre, and attendre, répondre and vendre in the present to talk about work and classes.

items.en: -ir verbs like finir in the present

drills.explain: il / elle / le cours → finit (the t is silent).
In the plural, -ir verbs like choisir add -iss-: nous choisissons.
ils / elles → finissent: you hear the ss.

items.fr: prendre, comprendre, apprendre (je prends, nous prenons, ils prennent)
items.en: prendre and its family in the present

drills.explain: ils → prennent, with a double n.
apprendre works like prendre: nous apprenons (one n).
comprendre → je comprends, like je prends.

items.fr: attendre, répondre, vendre (j'attends, il attend, ils attendent)

drills.explain: il → vend: just the stem, no ending.
attendre already means *wait for*: no pour. And je → attends, with an s.

items.note: No pour: attendre quelqu'un, attendre le bus.
répondre à: répondre à la question, au téléphone.
In Canada, an email is un courriel.

blocks.title: An evening French class in Montréal
blocks.context: Camille, the teacher, talks with Karim and Amira at the end of the class.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.en: Do you understand the question, Karim?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Oui, je comprends. Mais je réponds en anglais ou en français ?
lines.en: Yes, I understand. But do I answer in English or in French?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: En français, s'il vous plaît ! Ici, nous apprenons le français.
lines.en: In French, please! Here, we're learning French.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Madame, à quelle heure est-ce que le cours finit ?
lines.en: Ma'am, what time does the class finish?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Il finit à neuf heures. Et ce soir, vous choisissez un thème pour votre présentation.
lines.en: It finishes at nine. And tonight, you choose a topic for your presentation.

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Moi, je choisis le thème du travail !
lines.en: I'm choosing the topic of work!

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Après le cours, je prends le métro. Tu prends le métro aussi, Karim ?
lines.en: After class, I take the metro. Do you take the metro too, Karim?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Non, j'attends l'autobus. Ma femme et mes enfants attendent à la maison !
lines.en: No, I wait for the bus. My wife and children are waiting at home!

blocks.title: Nguyen at work
blocks.fr: Nguyen est vendeur dans un magasin d'électronique à Toronto. Il vend des téléphones et des ordinateurs. Il répond aux questions des clients et aux courriels. Il finit à dix-huit heures, mais ses collègues finissent à vingt heures. Le soir, il apprend le français.
blocks.en: Nguyen is a salesperson in an electronics store in Toronto. He sells phones and computers. He answers customers' questions and emails. He finishes at 6 p.m., but his colleagues finish at 8 p.m. In the evening, he learns French.

blocks.title: Not every verb ends in -er
blocks.body:
You already know many **-er** verbs ([[parler]], [[travailler]]). Today, three new families. Learn one model verb for each, and the others follow the same pattern:

- **finir** → [[choisir]]
- **prendre** → [[comprendre]], [[apprendre]]
- **attendre** → [[répondre]], [[vendre]]

Good news: in all three families, **je, tu, il / elle** sound the same. The difference is in the plural.

blocks.title: Finir and choisir
head: finir
choisir
blocks.note: The plural adds **-iss-**: [[nous finissons]], [[ils finissent]]. The final s and t of [[finis]], [[finit]] are silent.

blocks.title: Prendre, comprendre, apprendre
head: prendre
comprendre
apprendre
blocks.note: The d disappears in the plural. Watch the n: **one n** with nous and vous ([[prenons]], [[prenez]]), **two n** with ils ([[prennent]]). You already know [[je vais prendre…]] from the café; now you have the whole verb.

blocks.title: Attendre, répondre, vendre
head: attendre
répondre
vendre
blocks.note: Remove **-re** to get the stem ([[attend-]]), then add **-s, -s, nothing, -ons, -ez, -ent**. With il / elle, there is **no t**: [[il attend]], [[elle vend]].

blocks.title: Verbs and phrases in this lesson
Hear one or many
blocks.body:
Because [[il finit]] and [[ils finissent]] are spelled differently but [[il]] and [[ils]] sound the same, the **verb** tells you how many people:

- [[il finit]] (*fi-ni*) / [[ils finissent]] (*fi-niss*)
- [[elle prend]] (*pran*) / [[elles prennent]] (*prenn*)
- [[il attend]] (*a-tan*) / [[ils attendent]] (*a-tand*)

In the plural you hear an extra consonant at the end. The verb ending **-ent** is always silent.

- [[J'attends pour le bus]] → [[J'attends le bus]]. Attendre already contains *for*.
- [[Je réponds la question]] → [[Je réponds à la question]]. Répondre needs **à**: [[répondre au téléphone]], [[répondre aux courriels]].
- [[Ils prendent]] → [[Ils prennent]]. And [[nous prennons]] → [[nous prenons]].
- [[Nous finons]] → [[Nous finissons]]. Don't forget **-iss-**.
- [[Il attendt]] → [[Il attend]]. No ending at all with il / elle.

blocks.title: Courriel, the Canadian word for email
blocks.body:
In Canada, an email is [[un courriel]], a blend of *courrier électronique* (electronic mail). The word was popularized and recommended by the Office québécois de la langue française in the late 1990s, and it is now the normal word in Québec, in Canadian government services and at work: [[Je réponds aux courriels]], [[Envoyez-moi un courriel]]. In France, people mostly say [[un mail]] or [[un e-mail]].

Also notice Karim's [[l'autobus]]: in Québec, a city bus is often [[l'autobus]] (or [[le bus]] in conversation).

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Pay attention to the extra sound in the plural.

lines.fr: Elle prend le métro. Elles prennent le métro.
lines.en: She takes the metro. They take the metro.

lines.tip: A phrase you have known since unit 1, now with the whole verb behind it.

blocks.prompt: How many people finish at five?
How many people answer the phone?
blocks.explain: *ré-pon*, with no d sound: [[il répond]]. The plural would be *ré-pond*: [[ils répondent]].

blocks.explain: Two people = ils → prennent, with two n.
je → apprends; j' because apprends starts with a vowel.
vous → comprenez. Intonation, est-ce que or inversion are all correct.
attendre = to wait for; no pour.
optionFeedback: attendre already means *wait for*: no pour.
Before a vowel, je becomes j'.

blocks.prompt: Match each verb to its meaning.

blocks.explain: elle → répond (no t); répondre à + les courriels → aux courriels.
vous → [[finissez]], with -iss-. A relaxed way to ask *What time do you finish?*

accept: Ils vendent du pain et des croissants.
Ils vendent des croissants et du pain.
blocks.explain: ils → vendent; du pain, des croissants (partitive and plural).

blocks.prompt: Describe a normal day at work or school using at least four of today's verbs: how you get there (prendre), what you learn or sell, who or what you answer, when you finish.

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Le matin, je prends l'autobus. Je suis vendeuse : je vends des vêtements et je réponds aux questions des clients. Je finis à dix-sept heures. Le soir, j'apprends le français. Je comprends beaucoup de mots maintenant !
models.en: In the morning, I take the bus. I'm a salesperson: I sell clothes and I answer customers' questions. I finish at 5 p.m. In the evening, I learn French. I understand a lot of words now!

blocks.prompt: Write 4 or 5 sentences about your job or your French class. Use at least four different verbs from this lesson, including one in the plural (nous or ils / elles).
checklist: At least four verbs from today
One sentence about learning or understanding

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je suis étudiant à Gatineau. Le cours commence à neuf heures et il finit à midi. Nous apprenons le français et nous répondons aux questions de la professeure. Mes amis et moi, nous prenons l'autobus ensemble. Je comprends bien la professeure !
models.en: I'm a student in Gatineau. The class starts at nine and finishes at noon. We learn French and we answer the teacher's questions. My friends and I take the bus together. I understand the teacher well!

summary:
- Conjugate **finir / choisir**: [[je finis, nous finissons, ils finissent]]
- Conjugate **prendre / comprendre / apprendre**: [[je prends, nous prenons, ils prennent]]
- Conjugate **attendre / répondre / vendre**: [[j'attends, il attend, ils attendent]]
- Say [[J'attends le bus]] (no pour) and [[Je réponds aux courriels]] (with à)
